summary.headline: Varmora Granito Q2 FY27 utilisation rose to 89% and H1 PAT jumped 498% YoY, driven by a 17% price hike and better GVT mix.
summary.overview: This was the company's first earnings call after its 29 September 2026 listing. Management attributed the Q2 margin rebound to a 21% rise in average realisation (about 17% price hike, 3.5% mix) plus operating efficiency, after a disrupted Q1 when production stopped in April due to fuel unavailability. Exports fell sharply on container and freight shortages, while domestic GVT volumes grew. Management guided to around 15% value and 10% volume growth for FY27 if exports revive, and said no major capex is planned.

YoY; Q1 gross margin improved 8% as stated

financial_highlights.value: 17.63 MSM total, of which exports 3.42 MSM (H1 FY26); 15.04 MSM total, exports 2.03 MSM (H1 FY27)
INR9 crore in H1 FY27 vs INR60 crore in H1 FY26
1.9% of revenue in H1, guided flat for full year

segments.name: Domestic
segments.commentary: Domestic revenue grew 9% YoY excluding Simola; domestic GVT volume grew 14%. Domestic mix is about 82% GVT and 18% PVT/ceramics, and it is about 80% of total sales on a four-year average.

segments.name: Exports
segments.commentary: Export revenue fell about 17-18% YoY on container and freight unavailability. Export GVT share is about 98%, and sales are branded only with no white-label business. Export share in H1 FY27 was about 13% of volume (2.03 of 15.04 MSM).

segments.name: Product mix
segments.commentary: H1 FY27 mix is 82% GVT, 9% PVT and 8% ceramic, versus 75%, 14% and 11% in H1 FY26. Bathware is about 10% of revenue.

segments.name: Northeast / East plant
segments.commentary: Assam plant started, running at 50% utilisation in the last quarter and guided to 75% in Q3 and 85-87% in Q4. It makes only 2x2 and 4x2 GVT, and the East region contributes about 3% of revenue per management, against about 13-14% per the analyst's reading of the investor map.

guidance_outlook: FY27 revenue growth of around 15% in value and 10% in volume if exports revive, outperforming industry by 2-3%.
Q3 and Q4 margins expected to be better than Q2 margins, with utilisation moving from 76% toward 80-85% in FY28.
No price hike planned now: input costs are up 14-15% against a 17% cumulative price hike, leaving about 3% headroom.
Export freight is expected to fall from next month, with availability improving.
About 6.4 million sq m of additional capacity expected next year from the East plant. No immediate new capacity plans otherwise.
capex_capacity: Installed capacity is 50.6 million sq m, with H1 FY27 utilisation of 76% and peak utilisation up to 92-93%.
No immediate capex plan; maintenance capex is INR9-10 crore for the year.
Industry: 10-11 PVT and ceramic plants have shut in Morbi and 3-4 new lines are added, so there was no net capacity addition in H1. Three to four new lines are expected in Q1 FY28.
Integrated Stone Technology (IST) line with continuous press is operating, and there is no current plan for continuous press in other plants.
Northeast plant started, with product launched and dispatches begun. Benefits include CGST/SGST, interest subvention and a minimum capital subsidy.
demand_pricing: Average realisation rose INR75 YoY in Q2, with about 21% growth from INR50 price hike and INR25 mix.
Price hikes: about 14% in Q1 and 3-3.5% in Q2, a cumulative 17%.
Gas (propane) averaged INR84.73/SCM in Q1 and INR80.53 in Q2 in Morbi; current price is about INR92-93.
Bathware industry price hikes: about 25% for faucets and 17% for sanitaryware YoY. Management says Varmora is the second-highest average realisation among listed peers.
Export demand was constrained by container availability and freight. US freight was INR7,000-7,500 last month and INR5,500 this month, per management.

qa_highlights.question: What drove the Q2 margin improvement, and is it sustainable?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed it to the price hike and a mix shift toward larger GVT sizes (6x4 and 8x4), plus 89% utilisation in Q2. It said Q3 and Q4 margins should be better than Q2.

qa_highlights.question: Why did the depreciation policy change?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the company moved from WDV to SLM and changed the useful life from 15 to 10 years, with about INR14 crore PAT impact. It cited industry practice and capex needed for multi-size production.

qa_highlights.question: How much of the portfolio is outsourced, and how is gas pricing compared with Kajaria?
qa_highlights.answer: 14% is outsourced, mainly low-margin PVT and ceramic. Management said the gas-price comparison must account for calorific value, with propane at about 11,000 kcal against about 8,300 kcal for Gujarat Gas.

qa_highlights.question: What is the status of the IST product and its pricing?
qa_highlights.answer: IST is a full-body replica of natural marble, and management said it is India's first. It starts at INR300 per sq ft ex-factory and reaches about INR500-600 for consumers, against INR4,000-6,000 for natural Statuario marble.

qa_highlights.question: Are exports recovering, and is the company shifting away from them?
qa_highlights.answer: Management expects freight and availability to improve from next month. It said the export/domestic split has averaged about 80:20 over four years and will stay that way for the next 2-3 years.

risks_watch: Gas price volatility: Morbi propane rose to about INR92-93/SCM, and management has only about 3% pricing headroom.
Export recovery depends on container availability and freight, and exports fell 17-18% in H1.
Simola divestment removes about INR9 crore H1 revenue versus INR60 crore a year ago, and the East plant ramp-up is still early (50% utilisation).
Q3 Northeast margins are not yet disclosed; management will give numbers after Q3.
H1 volumes were down about 15% YoY, so price-led growth may be hard to sustain if volume does not recover.
summary.management_tone: Confident on margins and product mix, with specific figures given for utilisation and pricing. More cautious on exports and the macro backdrop, and several answers were left open (Northeast margins, the East-region revenue share and the Assam cost structure).
key_quotes: The second quarter was, in a way, you can say, a recovery quarter in which we registered very good growth.
Both benefits are sustainable, and I feel that better margins than this will come because the margins you saw for the first half had the disruption in Q1, and Q2 is better.
IST is the 100% replica of natural marble.

adds.what: Northeast/Assam GVT plant (2x2 and 4x2 GVT), started; about 6.4 million sq m additional capacity expected next year from East plant

growth.why: Management guides ~15% value and ~10% volume growth for FY27 conditional on export revival, backed partly by the Assam plant ramping to 75% in Q3 and 85-87% in Q4 and by realisation gains, while exports fell ~17-18% and H1 volume was down ~15%.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: Q2 realisation rose 21% (17% cumulative price hike plus 3.5% mix) and utilisation hit 89%, but input costs are up 14-15%, gas has risen to INR92-93/SCM, and pricing headroom is only about 3%, so the margin gain may not hold.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.when: Q3 FY27 to Q4 FY27 ramp; ~6.4 MSM additional East plant capa
rows.why: Assam plant started, running at 50% last quarter and guided to 75% in Q3 and 85-87% in Q4; management expects about 6.4 million sq m of additional capacity from the East plant next year, though H1 installed capacity is 50.6 MSM and no further plans are named.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Management guides about 10% volume growth for FY27 if exports revive, with Assam ramping from 50% to 75% in Q3 and 85-87% in Q4 and utilisation moving from 76% toward 80-85% in FY28; but H1 volume was down about 15% and exports fell 17-18%.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Management says there is no immediate capex plan and maintenance capex is only INR9-10 crore for FY27, even though utilisation is 89% in Q2 and 76% in H1 with peaks of 92-93%; the company is relying on the Assam ramp rather than new capex.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Management expects Q3 and Q4 margins to be better than Q2 and freight is falling (US freight INR7,000-7,500 last month, INR5,500 this month), but the upgrade hinges on export volumes recovering, which is not yet visible.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: FY27 guide of ~15% value and ~10% volume depends on export revival, while exports fell 17-18% in H1, H1 volume was down about 15% YoY (15.04 vs 17.63 MSM), and gas is rising to INR92-93/SCM against only about 3% pricing headroom.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: IST (full-body replica marble, launched at INR300/sq ft ex-factory) is already operating on a continuous press line, but no further product launch timing is given and there is no plan for continuous press at other plants.

rows.label: No further price hike; about 3% headroom
rows.why: Input costs are up 14-15% against a 17% cumulative price hike, leaving only about 3% headroom, and management has said no price hike is planned now.

rows.label: Export recovery from freight and container easing
rows.why: Management expects export freight to fall from next month, with US freight down from INR7,000-7,500 to INR5,500, but exports were down 17-18% YoY and export share is only about 13% of H1 volume (2.03 of 15.04 MSM).

rows.label: Simola divestment drags reported revenue
rows.why: Simola revenue fell to INR9 crore in H1 FY27 from INR60 crore in H1 FY26, a divested entity that will keep weighing on reported growth comparisons.

tone.note: Management was confident on Q2 pricing, mix and margin direction and gave specific utilisation and cost numbers, but was more cautious on exports, the macro backdrop and the Northeast plant's margins and cost structure; analysts pressed on the depreciation policy change, gas-price comparisons with K
